posts.title: Find failures in AI agent traces
posts.promise: Flag suspicious runs and investigate why an AI agent may have failed.
posts.whatItIs: Tessary is an open-source reliability platform for AI agents, according to its co-founder. It watches production traces, meaning records of an agent's steps, and uses a first layer of classifiers to flag traces that may contain errors. A second layer of agents investigates flagged traces for possible causes. A small student version could accept saved traces from one test agent, apply a few simple error checks, and ask a model to summarize flagged cases. Developers building AI agents might pay for this kind of monitoring, but the source gives no customer or revenue evidence. The repeatable loop can sort and investigate runs automatically; a person still needs to decide whether a flag is a real failure and whether a suggested fix is safe. The co-founder says the design grew from the high cost of evaluating agent behavior, but that explanation and any performance claims remain founder statements.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: teams operating AI agents may pay to find and investigate failures; the source does not establish customers or revenue.
loop: Collect a trace from an AI agent run.
Apply inexpensive classifiers to flag traces that may contain errors.
Send flagged traces to an investigation agent.
Summarize likely causes for a developer to review.
A human checks the finding and decides whether to change the agent.
posts.evidence: The co-founder describes Tessary as an open-source agent reliability platform that monitors every production trace, uses classifiers to flag potentially erroneous traces, and runs agents to triage and investigate causes. The maker's cost comparison is an attributed claim, not independently verified.
posts.uncertainty: The available evidence is a founder's Show HN description; it does not independently establish detection accuracy, customer adoption, or revenue. A student version could handle a small set of saved traces, but model summaries may be wrong and flags are not proof of a failure. A person should inspect the trace before changing a live agent.
first24Hours: Save several example traces from a test agent, including one with a known mistake.
Write simple rules to flag missing outputs or tool errors and store the flagged trace IDs.
Ask a language model to summarize one flagged trace, then compare its explanation with a human review.

steps.message: Compared nine snapshot candidates and existing published posts; selected Tessary for its clearly described trace monitoring and investigation loop, with founder claims and reliability limits stated explicitly.
